review_notes: Reviewed the current top-level proposal.json, not merely the proposal embedded in the prior-result packet. Read all 115 proposal lines, all 36 functionality lines, all 564 fact-ledger lines and all 614 link-ledger lines. Also read coverage.json and unresolved.json.

All four proposed writes are supported by canonical source and remain within owned subjects. The proposal correctly fixes the landing predicate's argument flow, replaces unsupported stronger-friction language, records consumed-event and constructor data flow, and distinguishes all three held-item entry cases.

Independently checked the common transition inlines, throw-bit inline, bomb constructor, physics helpers, animation predicate, neutral completion helper, common item-throw initializer, accessory callback dispatcher, adjacent item kinds and active Link/CLink motion-table consumers.

The current ledgers improve on the prior packet by explicitly deferring the ground-collision does-nothing claim, the hand-appearance game-mapping claim and three exact-placement link rationales. These deferrals are appropriate and are preserved below.

Acceptance does not prove compiled section layout, register allocation, exact bomb appearance timing, all collision preservation effects or complete callback/item ownership. No replacement proposal, new relational records or unowned writes are supplied.

Retained mechanic-level descriptions identify supported action responsibilities, not unconditional allocation success or Link-exclusive use. Numeric motion IDs 108 and 112 remain literal caller-selected IDs; their full gameplay classification is not inferred from enum names.

The rendered source has nine external name substitutions and no parse errors. Those aliases were treated as hypotheses, not independent evidence. Ambiguous doEnter/doAnim and the shadowed cb binding remain unchanged.

unresolved: All four .sdata2 facts remain unresolved. Source literals cannot establish compiled section bytes, size, ordering, references or exclusive consumers.
The eleven parameter subjects have no baseline facts. Their r3/r4 suffixes are not independently verified register allocations.

The full directional and throw-classification meaning of literal motion IDs 108 and 112 remains unproved through complete active common motion/throw table evidence. No proposed write assigns those gameplay names.

Collision predicate internal side effects and complete coll_mf preservation semantics, especially Unk19 and Unk27, remain unresolved. The three baseline collision facts containing absolute no-change or preservation language are explicitly deferred.

Exact initial visible bomb position and appearance frame remain unresolved. The constructor copies the supplied vector into prev_pos and obtains pos separately. Two whole fact claims and three exact-placement link records are deferred; exact-thumb assertions appearing only in retained facts' historical rationales are also not adopted as proved.

The semantic role of fp->ft_data->x8->x10 beyond forwarding to Item_8026AB54 and the loaded numeric value of da->x48 remain unresolved. Constructor consumption of the fourth argument as SpawnItem.kind is proved.

Complete accessory4 reset rules, interruption/death cleanup, item destruction ownership and safety against a subsequently occupied held-item slot remain unresolved. Local absence of a held-slot recheck or callback self-unregistration does not establish that a conflicting overwrite occurs in ordinary gameplay.

Throw-bit script production and exact scheduling relative to all animation, collision and interruption paths remain unresolved. A true ftCheckThrowB0 consumes the event before the construction attempt, including a failed attempt.

Exceptional-float statements are source-level observations, not compiled-target verification. Friction positivity, multiplier strength, finite facing/positions and nonzero lifetime-minus-xC are not established. Ordinary deceleration descriptions are not universal invariants.

Detailed positioning, model-selection and pickup semantics are not independently established by rendered aliases. The accepted writes preserve canonical calls and exact argument/return flow rather than promoting those names.
Duplicate links and overlapping bomb, bomb-pull and bomb-down-special concepts remain separate exact records. No merge or new relational record is proposed.
